title: Sparse routing and prefix memory
intervention: Compare sparse access, capacity, and shared initialization.
finding: Local changes did not yield a stable broad advantage; fewer active parameters are not a substitute for comparing capability.

title: Character, subword, and morphological pathways
intervention: Distinguish auxiliary word-form structure from capacity effects and lookup controls.
finding: Surface-information gains in limited settings have not become a stable broad advantage across seeds.

title: Whole-word and token masking
intervention: Compare masking granularity against a fixed training reference, examining paired seeds and individual task scores.
finding: Granularity changes task trade-offs, supporting specific training choices but not a uniform ranking across all capabilities.

title: Backbone architecture and batch-size controls
intervention: Compare BERT- and DeBERTa-style configurations and check batch-size differences.
finding: The late-training advantage of the combined configuration cannot be explained by batch size alone; the contributions of position-related components have not been independently isolated.

title: Recursive autoregressive training
intervention: Reproduce the recursive training scheme, complete the corresponding evaluation, and check word coverage.
finding: This setting did not match the leading configuration; word-coverage differences cannot explain the entire performance gap.

title: Vocabulary, depth, width, and budget
intervention: Compare vocabulary sizes and depth-width configurations, distinguishing prototypes from budget-compliant retraining.
finding: Higher tokenization compression ratios did not automatically yield stable gains; the actual training budget must also be accounted for.

title: Frequency gating and fine-grained representations
intervention: Let coarse-grained word representations draw on fine-grained units and check the zero-gate limit.
finding: The limiting implementation behaves as expected, but trained models were not stronger; other gates and seeds remain candidates.

title: Components of a mature training recipe
intervention: Examine depth, width, vocabulary, LAMB, and sequence-length and masking curricula.
finding: No single component reproduced the full configuration's performance; interactions among components must also be studied.

title: Gated feed-forward and layer-weighting candidates
intervention: Retain proposed designs for GEGLU, attention gating, and layer weighting.
finding: These are candidates, not validated methods, and do not count as empirical model contributions.

title: Aligned reformulation and correspondence
intervention: Compare correct and incorrect correspondence, matched sources, repetition, and split windows.
finding: Relational organization changes learning, but benefits depend on the task; follow-up studies in the main text further distinguish target types.

title: Compact views and budget reinvestment
intervention: Compress the second view and use the freed word budget for more pairs.
finding: Experience coverage increased, yielding a practical frontier-model method; the effects of compression and expanded coverage must be distinguished.

title: Adjacency, repetition, and presentation layout
intervention: Compare content and adjacency effects, examining block and interleaved presentation.
finding: Effects differ across capabilities; tokenizers and window settings must be matched.

title: Extractive compression and bridging text
intervention: Construct bridging texts with balanced coverage, broader coverage, and controlled lexical scope.
finding: Word coverage can be checked, but it is not a substitute for semantic relations or gains in the complete model.

title: Rule-based rewriting
intervention: Compare true pairs, same-entity mismatches, source-only controls, and shuffled controls.
finding: Short-run results showed capability trade-offs, not joint gains; visible token counts still need to be matched.

title: Entity-mention consistency
intervention: Compare correct correspondence, incorrect correspondence, and ordinary whole-word masking.
finding: Local advantages from correct correspondence did not reliably translate into broad capability gains.

title: Counterfactual and cross-span supervision
intervention: Compare true-relation, wrong-relation, and no-relation conditions, checking existing capabilities.
finding: An identifiable relation effect is a different conclusion from learning a relation from scratch.

title: State text and directed masking
intervention: Construct training texts and target-position controls around state selection.
finding: Target behavior can improve while broad language performance degrades, motivating joint tests of new learning and retention.

title: Auxiliary causal objectives
intervention: Match shifted targets and gradient norms, comparing batch replacement with auxiliary learning.
finding: Similarly directed gradients did not guarantee full-model improvement; local gradient relationships do not establish a general rule for training outcomes.

title: Self-sampled replaced-token detection
intervention: Add a detection objective and decompose its gradient effects.
finding: Short-run aggregate scores showed both gains and costs; overall effectiveness in late training remains unconfirmed.

title: Target weighting and supervision coverage
intervention: Compare per-word averaging, coverage floors, and source-absent content weighting.
finding: Local fit can improve at the cost of broader performance; replacement under an equal target budget still needs separate testing.

title: Relational pivots and counterfactual cues
intervention: Match supervision quantity and distinguish relational selection from direct retrieval.
finding: If retrieval still solves the task, high scores cannot establish a new computation for state selection.

title: Gradient exchange and projection
intervention: Use centered four-condition comparisons, directional projection, and negative examples.
finding: Local gradient differences have been observed, but long-term training gains have not been established.

title: Coherent-context margin loss
intervention: Compare against negatives with disrupted context and examine late-stage continuation.
finding: The expected behavioral separation was not obtained; the zero-coefficient comparison was not completed, so the result cannot be fully attributed to a single factor.

title: Adaptive masking granularity
intervention: Compare data-objective combinations along training trajectories.
finding: Early rankings can reverse; the learning stage must be considered when judging a training scheme.

title: Data order and developmental curricula
intervention: Use random and developmental orderings of the same content and correct truncation.
finding: An effective combined scheme does not establish a universal advantage for curriculum ordering.

title: Context-length caps
intervention: Hold paired-example exposure fixed while comparing length caps and evaluation lengths.
finding: The observed Overall change is affected by the AoA reference; the seven task families did not improve simultaneously.

title: Optimizers and mature model states
intervention: Compare AdamW, LAMB, optimizer switches at maturity, and trust ratios.
finding: Local numerical changes during optimization have not yet been shown to predict late-training model outcomes.

title: Checkpoint averaging and restarts
intervention: Compare averaging adjacent checkpoints, restarts, and another seed.
finding: Averaging did not reliably improve on individual high-scoring models; model selection and methodological attribution must be separated.

title: Relation dose and learning maturity
intervention: Compare concentrated, sparse, and role-changing binding experience.
finding: Constructed tasks can be learned, but natural-text training with a weak base and sparse exposure did not automatically reproduce the capability; additional budget is listed separately.

title: Continued relation-training candidates
intervention: Retain proposals for continued relation losses, switching between local and full context, and remention masking.
finding: These remain routes to test, not achieved results.

title: Zero-initialized bottleneck branch
intervention: Check shared parameters, disabled-branch controls, and training trajectories.
finding: The branch preserves the base function at initialization and when disabled; joint training still updates the base.

title: Main and auxiliary path separation
intervention: Move from broad to sparse auxiliary learning, including comparisons with the auxiliary branch disabled on the main path.
finding: Early gains did not carry over directly to mature models, motivating ordinary coherent replay.

title: Dedicated increments on a frozen base
intervention: Train only newly added parameters, using ordinary prediction and KL; compare coherent and disrupted inputs.
finding: This produced the first-generation model; disabling the branch restores the base, but retention with it enabled still requires evaluation.

title: Model lineage and scale selection
intervention: Distinguish continuous-packing branches, the main model, incremental branches, and the inference scale used for release.
finding: Actual weight inheritance does not mean that every research route entered the final model in sequence.

title: Writing and reading with supplied addresses
intervention: Compare consistent address permutations, wrong addresses, overwrites, and slot swaps.
finding: Stored signals have a functional role; results using gold-standard addresses do not establish natural-language addressing.

title: Answer shortcuts in a tiny binding task
intervention: Subsequent checks found that answers did not change with the queried entity.
finding: The original high scores no longer support compositional binding; correcting the corpus is not equivalent to verification by retraining.

title: Routing from natural text to addresses
intervention: Compare raw-text, lexical, recurrent, and discrete routing with correct supplied addresses.
finding: High aggregate token accuracy concealed zero recall on critical queries, identifying an addressing bottleneck.

title: Pointer and copy initialization
intervention: Test initialization for small pointer models, embeddings, and copying behavior.
finding: Being able to copy does not mean being able to select the correct entity state.

title: Format preadaptation and label alignment
intervention: Compare preparatory training with aligned, shuffled, and unrelated labels.
finding: Several forms of preparation can help subsequent learning, so the benefit cannot be attributed solely to one particular correspondence signal.

title: Frozen readers and within-group selection
intervention: Train selection using a four-candidate within-group softmax, measuring lexical, role, and temporal semantics separately.
finding: Lexical matching and role swaps were nearly fully successful, but selecting prior versus updated states remained weak.

title: Identifiability of relational rules
intervention: Vary the initial owner and construct balanced counterexamples.
finding: High training scores may reflect an anti-copy shortcut; counterfactuals help identify the intended rule.

title: Binary relation graphs and sparse anchors
intervention: Compare shared and separate representations, reverse anchors, and measure whether relative relations are preserved, using multiple training seeds.
finding: Absolute orientation can propagate along shared paths while relative relations are preserved; the conclusion is limited to the given hypothesis class.

title: Character identity and access to relational structure
intervention: Learn matching from letter-equality supervision, then connect it to shared relational structure.
finding: Coverage of the base alphabet supports new combinations; candidates and hard assignments are supplied, and edge deletion also changes the training amount.

title: Leakage-free graph and program construction
intervention: Generate neutral, reversed, and program-structured tasks, checking categories and priors.
finding: Candidate yield and type balance remain limited; prototypes do not establish general reasoning ability.

title: Structural density and representation recovery
intervention: Compare structural densities, residualized conditions, and random controls.
finding: Recovery of local structural readouts did not guarantee broad gains and must not be conflated with capacity.

title: Tail training on shared-source clusters
intervention: Compare true, shuffled, repeated, and ordinary experience.
finding: Outperforming mismatched controls does not mean outperforming all references; model measurements are incomplete.

title: Views, breadth, and repetition under a fixed budget
intervention: Replace training experience under a common budget and retain multiple late-stage models.
finding: Late-stage gains depend on experience type and architecture; adding distinct sentences is not equivalent to adding documents.

title: Register substitution and data-value prediction
intervention: Hold added content fixed, vary the displaced register, and compare word distributions and task scores.
finding: Opportunity costs differ with the material displaced; results from different measurement settings cannot directly validate the same prediction.

title: Selecting explicit relational text
intervention: Compare explicit relational text with random quality controls and filter natural state text.
finding: Qualified candidates are limited; short-run results cannot be treated as a mature large-scale training stream.

title: Deletion of source-absent and copied targets
intervention: Keep inputs fixed and nearly match the number of deleted targets, using source-pair-disjoint and document-disjoint splits.
finding: Local source-pair results hold, but intervals under stricter document separation cross zero; rankings on the full task set differ.

title: Correct, wrong, and missing sources
intervention: Hold target tokens fixed and vary source conditions.
finding: Source effects can exist without added supervision and cannot directly be treated as the cause of final-model improvement.

title: Coverage, order, and local context
intervention: Distinguish source presence, prefix placement, gaps, and relative text positions within windows.
finding: Comparisons with incompletely verified model-loading identity illustrate context geometry only; they do not confirm specific mechanism effects.

title: Ordered composition and dynamic binding
intervention: Compare dynamic and static relations, local and final supervision, and examine readouts.
finding: Information decodable from representations is not necessarily a computation the model actually performs.

title: Contextual hidden states and interventions
intervention: Compare consistent prefixes, mismatches, entity substitutions, and activation replacements.
finding: Topic information can be present even when state-dependent execution fails; behavioral and functional tests are both needed.

title: State updates in microworlds
intervention: Control states, actions, contradictions, answer cues, and overwrites.
finding: These provide diagnostic tools, not automatic evidence that the same selector has formed in natural text.

title: Gradient conflict and learning-signal estimation
intervention: Use comparisons with identical materials, across pairs, and with held-out objects.
finding: Local correlations have not become stable prospective predictors of learning gains.

title: Contrastive prediction and auxiliary readouts
intervention: Compare same-source, cross-source, and hard-negative conditions.
finding: Fitting or saturating an auxiliary objective is insufficient evidence that new capability has formed.

title: Layer-wise readouts and position editing
intervention: Use bilinear and ridge-regression readouts, rotated-null controls, and local edits.
finding: Local fit does not guarantee held-out transfer; limited editing examples do not support broad mechanistic conclusions.

title: Score changes under pair swaps
intervention: Check matching conditions including categories, shuffling, and length swaps.
finding: Algebraic cancellation in scores does not mean that the model actually used the correspondence.

title: Shared-parameter initialization
intervention: Explicitly copy shared tensors and separately measure architectures' absolute capability and the relative effects of data.
finding: The same random seed does not guarantee identical initial values; after correction, evidence for a large interaction was substantially weakened.

title: Macro averages and item-level changes
intervention: Compute gains, losses, net changes, and complementary items separately.
finding: Macro averages and net changes in the number of correct answers can have opposite signs; one aggregate score cannot fully describe capability changes.

title: Transfer conditions and representation geometry
intervention: Compare seed conditions, principal components, and random controls.
finding: Correlations and radial growth have not established capability conservation or a universal law of transfer.

title: Complete evaluation and model interfaces
intervention: Verify the loading implementation, AoA trajectories, and commonsense-task and Reading scoring.
finding: Missing measurements, zero scores, and publicly displayed values are treated separately; complete model identity determines comparability.

title: Word boundaries, packing, and visible budgets
intervention: Check pair integrity, truncation, and actual presentation in continuous windows.
finding: Accounted word counts must correspond to visible content; prototype and final tokenizer implementations must not be mixed.

title: Microbatches and gradient equivalence
intervention: Weight by target count and compare gradients before and after activation recomputation under fixed randomness.
finding: These checks validate limited implementation conditions, not exact identity of complete stochastic training trajectories.

title: Model reconstruction and cost breakdown
intervention: Fix the identities of weights, configuration, and code, separating training from search costs.
finding: Same-seed reconstruction, replication across seeds, and compute savings are distinct conclusions.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Selectivity in relation learning
intervention: Compare source advantages from verbatim repetition and aligned reformulation across three seeds.
finding: The effects on compact reformulation targets differ in direction and do not imply that repetition is universally harmful.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Prediction windows with matched materials
intervention: Split repetition pairs and reformulation pairs into separate windows in their respective conditions.
finding: The large source effects were substantially attenuated; content is matched between the same-window and split-window versions of each pairing condition.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Transfer conditions for natural reformulations
intervention: Group natural-restatement targets by whether their exact tokenizer ID appears in the source.
finding: Aligned restatement improves source use for recurring target tokens; nonrecurring targets show no equally stable improvement over the reference. This distinction is lexical, not a definition of semantic novelty.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Familiar performance and functional access with unseen symbols
intervention: Compare ordinary continuation, statically weighted supervision, and interleaved supervision.
finding: Recovery of familiar behavior does not guarantee restored functional reach for unseen symbols.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Erasing and relocating functional signals
intervention: Center, zero, and rotate attribute-position signals, and test refitted directions.
finding: The results support the functional role of a specific signal; unsuccessful recovery using linear directions does not rule out all distributed recoding.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Dense inputs and sparse supervision
intervention: Reuse existing text while controlling masking candidates and focused targets separately.
finding: At equal exposure, complete evaluations for both seeds outperformed ordinary continuation; the comparison does not isolate masking as a single factor.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Preservation inputs and effective strength
intervention: Measure preservation gradients at fixed shared target positions and compare ordinary and dense inputs.
finding: With the same coefficient, gradient magnitudes still differ by a factor of approximately 12; the full comparison also changes the set of target positions.

group: Core research: extensions and empirical tests
title: Principle-guided complete model
intervention: Recheck ordinary continuation, relation learning, and the complete preservation scheme from the same parent model.
finding: The complete scheme improved the nine-task Overall score for both continuation seeds; additional exposure and compute are reported separately.
